title: shellcheck reaches a change only at the release cut: no test runs the lint gate
body:
## Problem

shellcheck reaches a change only at the release cut. At the 0.1.8 cut on 2026-09-26, six patches (0134, 0135, 0145, 0148, 0149, 0150) had each converged under critic-shell, passed their targeted runs and mutant batches, and passed the whole suite on the exact landing tree. The cut's `check all` lint then found SC2034 in `lib/cmd/fullcycle` (0150) and SC2004 in `lib/runlog` (0135), and both were fixed mid-cut at b4eed88. Nothing shipped wrong, but a release commit already made had to wait on a fix-up.

Lint is in no loop a change passes through before landing:

- no arm under `tests/` runs the lint gate (`git grep` finds no test naming `shell-gate lint` or `check lint`), so targeted runs, mutant batches and the suite are all blind to it;
- the pre-commit hook runs Intent's gate (guards, critic, doctor), not devbin's lint;
- critic-shell reads the rule library, which overlaps shellcheck without being it, and it passed both lines;
- build stacks live in scratch clones, which carry no hooks;
- `check all` runs at the cut and on CI after a push, both after landing.

The same gap showed in review on 2026-10-03: 0152's comment-only rewrite is proven code-same by `shfmt -mn`, which drops `# shellcheck` directives with every other comment, so only shellcheck itself can see an edited directive.

## Measured (cc, 2026-10-03)

`bin/devbin check lint` over 0152 v1's patched tree: 48 files, 0 breaches, 68 seconds of wall clock (16:34:48Z to 16:35:56Z by `date -u`). `gate_lint` in `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate` runs `shellcheck -x` once per file, in series, and `-x` follows `source` into `lib/helpers` for every file that sources it.

## Fix

1. One lint definition, reached from the suite: a `contract.bats` arm runs `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate lint`, the command `check lint` itself runs, over the tree under test, and asserts a clean exit. `contract.bats` is already in every targeted run. Where shellcheck is absent the arm skips and says what was not checked; both CI legs have it.
2. Fast enough to sit in every targeted run: measured off a booked slot, one invocation over all the files and a parallel run against today's file-at-a-time loop. The fastest that keeps a per-file verdict goes into `shell-gate` itself, so `check lint` and CI gain it too.

This adds a test to the suite and gates nothing new: no release waits on it.

## Done when

1. An SC2034 planted in a copy of the tree turns the arm red, and the clean tree is green.
2. The arm reports how many files it linted, holds a floor, and skips with a reason when shellcheck is missing.
3. The time it adds to a targeted run is measured, and the numbers are in the landing commit.

## Resolution

Fixed at 9aebdf0c. The suite now runs the lint gate `check lint` runs: contract.bats runs `bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate lint` over the tree under test and holds a clean verdict over at least 40 files, so shellcheck reaches a change in every targeted run that includes contract.bats, before it lands rather than at the cut. gate_lint runs `shellcheck -x` in parallel, jobs from nproc or getconf capped at 8, each file's output and status kept apart and read back in corpus order; a worker that dies is named as a file with no verdict and counted a breach, the summary still prints, and the scratch is removed.

Against the done-when list:

1. An SC2034 planted in a two-file probe tree turns the gate red, naming the code and counting one breach, and the clean tree is green: contract.bats's first (0155) arm, the probe being its positive control.
2. The arm prints how many files it linted, holds a floor of 40, and skips saying the lint gate was not run when shellcheck is missing.
3. The arm adds 12.6 s and 12.4 s to a targeted run that includes contract.bats (two runs in a quiet window, 16 CPUs, at a3f649f4); gate_lint over the tree, 48 files, takes 12.8 s and 12.4 s in parallel (8 jobs, its cap) against 76.6 s and 77.2 s serial. The numbers are in the landing commit.

Evidence. 5 mutants over shell-gate, all killed; a second arm kills a worker mid-run with a fake shellcheck and holds the no-verdict line, the summary and the empty scratch. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as the BSD tools. The full suite on the landing tree: vc's full suite, on main af758c10 (code at 415ce738) with 0163 v3.1 and 0167 git-am'd and cc's 0155, 0160, 0161 and 0162 applied above them, in a fresh clone: 2190 of 2190 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261006-0607), 06:07:26Z to 06:55:27Z; 5 skipped, the expected five: two arms that need a runner with no controlling terminal, two require_command arms whose expected outcome is a skip, and a case-folding disk.
